scope: Unicode launch-argument prerequisite; not managed-generation or daily desktop acceptance
source: 3deedcd with the accompanying fixed UTF-8 Linux runtime-binding change

environment.userspace: Independent pinned Arch chroot, Wine 11.14 x86_64
environment.display: Private Xvfb 1280x800x24; no user desktop modified
environment.isolation: Mount, PID and network namespaces, tini PID 1, ordinary UID 1000

observations.detail: All three applications started but could not open Chinese file paths. Dialogs showed corrupted file names. The supervised process environment had no LANG or LC_ALL after env_clear.
Changing only request LANG and LC_ALL to C.UTF-8 allowed all three applications to open the same existing fixtures.

Regenerated contexts using the fixed provider; requests supplied DISPLAY only. 7-Zip displayed the archive, Notepad++ displayed the UTF-8 BOM Chinese text, and SumatraPDF displayed page 1 of the PDF. All service sessions exited successfully after joined cleanup.

checks.red: Existing fixed-binding equality test failed after adding expected LANG/LC_ALL values before changing the provider
checks.green: Actual Linux provider: 85 unit tests and 6 DXVK integration tests passed; clippy all-targets with -D warnings passed
checks.requestOverride: Planner regression verifies Chinese, spaces and percent arguments survive and request LANG=C/LC_ALL=C cannot replace the fixed binding

remaining: Some Chinese labels in 7-Zip lists and Notepad++ tabs still show missing-glyph boxes; font fallback is not fixed by the locale change
Existing serialized contexts must be regenerated to acquire the new binding
File save, managed lifecycle, desktop launch, reboot persistence and complete Chinese input remain separate acceptance gates
